### Home stops working when nothing is happening
The status dot on the Safe Internet card was animating forever, whether or not the app was even in front of you. One small dot was costing about a third of a processor core, all day, because every frame of it re-laid out the whole window. It is a static icon now, and the progress bar on the Blocking screen has stopped breathing while you are somewhere else. Expect a quieter fan and a longer battery.
### A blocked page stays in the tab
Opening YouTube Shorts on a Mac where it is turned off could black out the whole screen instead of showing the explanation inside the tab, which read less like a rule and more like the Mac had been taken over. The page now lands in the tab it belongs to. When there is genuinely no tab to put it in, the notice covers only the browser window, never the display — and it no longer describes a blocked website as an app.
### Signing out really does reset the Mac
Signing out left the Safe Internet filter installed but no longer recognised, so Home reported protection as off while the filter was quietly still running, and offered to set up something you already had. A sign-out now clears it properly and setup starts from the beginning, the filter included.
### For managed Macs
An organisation can now require Uninstall Protection, and turn it on for a device from the console. Setup asks for the administrator password once, so a change made later does not put a password box in front of whoever is holding the Mac.
If protection needs to come off and your organisation allows it, support can now issue an emergency code that removes it immediately, instead of a 24-hour wait.
